newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares recover to end only slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares recover to end only slightly lower.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares recovered from a weak opening to close only slightly easier on Monday. Major investors stayed away from the market but Swiss shares drew some support from the firmer dollar and from short covering.
Dealers said that although the market shrugged off Wall Street's losses the U.S. share market was likely to determine future developments.
* The blue-Chip SMI was down 17.9 to 4,586.3 after an intraday low of 4,537.3
* Broad SPI lost 10.97 to end at 2,906.88.
Roche, down 320 to 11,930, led the actives list.
Dealers said some investors sold Roche ahead of 1997 first quarter sales data, due for release on Tuesday. Roche is also holdubg its annual news conference on Tuesday.
Cement producer Holderbank, due to release 1996 results on Tuesday after the market closes, firmed seven francs to 1,128.
Several analysts recently issued "buy" recommendations for Holderbank although some expected a slight drop in its 1996 profit.
Nestle recouped early losses to close 17 francs higher at 1,717.
Cyclical shares were mixed to higher.

Among banks, UBS rose two to 1,309. Dealers said there was some buying ahead of the banks shareholder meeting on Thursday. CS group lost 2.25 francs to finish at 159.50. SBC eased 0.50 to close at 293.
Second tier shares saw strong gains in SEZ, Stratec, Belimo and Zellweger. Logitech, Zschokke, Agie and Valora were subject to profit taking.
Soffex trading saw rising implicit volatilities and the first roll-over transactions ahead of the Friday expiry.
Trade in options on Holderbank and UBS was active dealers said.
They said the SMI futures traded at or slightly above fair value.
The April SMI closed 12 points lower at 4,590 after the day's low of 4,535.
